subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw keep default steering as boundary-based behavior, or add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context?
rationale: The choice affects shared runtime semantics, user-visible channel behavior, Codex/native runtime integration, queue-mode compatibility, and how interrupt/followup fallback should behave.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steer semantics as the supported default and use #48003/#89238 only to ensure messages reach the existing boundary-based policy.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate explicit mode or command for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for partial output, tool calls, backend rejection, and fallback.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change default steer to the stronger lifecycle only after maintainer-approved upgrade proof and cross-runtime/channel compatibility coverage.

recommendation.title: Define soft-steer as an opt-in lifecycle
recommendation.body: Add or refresh a soft-steer queue/control path with explicit abort-or-pause, transcript, fallback, and proof requirements before changing default behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: The current issue and replacement PR history point to vincentkoc as the strongest owner for shared active-run steering and queue behavior.
